Russia has begun sabotage operations against Danish companies supplying Ukraine after concluding that broader disruption efforts failed to curb Western military support for the country, a Danish intelligence official said on Wednesday.
The shift reflects a significant escalation in Moscow's hybrid warfare campaign, Josefine Christensen, lead analyst at the Danish national security and intelligence service (PET), told a homeland security conference in Copenhagen.
"What we saw in the spring was a lot of planning, but very little carried out; what we saw in early summer is that they started to carry out a lot more," Christensen said.
Russia concluded that its previous broad-spectrum targeting "did not have the effect of deterring the Western [military alliance] NATO from supporting Ukraine," she said.

Germany’s federal prosecutor’s office has said a former domestic intelligence chief was arrested on Tuesday on espionage allegations.
August Hanning served as president of the Federal Intelligence Service (BND) from December 1998 to November 2005.
Hanning was arrested in Bad Toelz-Wolfratshausen, in southern Germany. A former aide of his, identified only as Manfred D, was also arrested on Tuesday.

Rozhlasové stanice WDR, MDR a list Süddeutsche Zeitung uvádějí, že Hanning je podezřelý, že nejméně v jednom případě vypracoval bezpečnostní analýzu pro cizí zpravodajskou službu. Nešlo podle nich o Rusko.
Podle zprávy státní zástupci tvrdí, že Hanning, jehož funkční období skončilo v roce 2005, koupil tajné informace od bývalého zaměstnance zahraniční rozvědky BND a měl v úmyslu je dále prodat v rámci své poradenské činnosti, píše Reuters.

The ship's captain was killed in the strike involving two drones, Zelensky said, and another sailor was unaccounted for. Eleven crew members - nationals of Azerbaijan and India - have been rescued.

Eight Russian officers were killed when a Tu-95MS missile-carrying bomber crashed in the Amur region on September 29. The independent Russian news outlet Mediazona published the full list of those on board.
The plane crashed near the village of Krasnoyarovo. Initial reports said six crew members were killed during a training flight from the Ukrainka air base.
A post about the unveiling of a memorial to the dead pilots later appeared on the “Rural News” community page for Seryshevo, a village in the Amur region where the Ukrainka air base is located. OSINT analyst duke garland noticed the post. Mediazona verified the information and found that all eight of those killed had served in strategic aviation.

shrnuti: A bomb destroyed a car belonging to a participant in Russia’s war against Ukraine on October 2 in Novomoskovsk, in Russia’s Tula region, the Ukrainian monitoring Telegram channel Exilenova+ reported.

Car bomb in Russia kills ex-prison official Ukraine accused of torturing POWs — Meduza
Skip to main content
Car bomb in Russia kills ex-prison official Ukraine accused of torturing POWs
October 5, 2026, 7:17 am
Source: Meduza
A bomb destroyed a car belonging to a participant in Russia’s war against Ukraine on October 2 in Novomoskovsk, in Russia’s Tula region, the Ukrainian monitoring Telegram channel Exilenova+ reported.
The bomb had been planted under the car’s chassis, according to  data from the anonymous Russian Telegram channel VChK-OGPU. The driver killed was identified as Roman Syromyatnikov, and the Novomoskovsk-based news outlet Novomoskovsk Segodnya confirmed the death of a person by that name.
Syromyatnikov worked at Russia’s Federal Penitentiary Service (FSIN) facilities in the Tula region during the 2010s. He signed a contract with Russia’s Defense Ministry in 2023 and returned to the Tula region for medical treatment in late 2024, the independent Russian investigative outlet iStories reported , citing leaked data.

September 23, 2026, 3:04 pm
Source: Operational Command of the Polish Armed Forces
A Russian military Mi-8 helicopter entered Polish airspace on September 23 at 11:08 a.m., the operational command of the Polish army said.
The helicopter, flying from the Kaliningrad region, crossed about 300 meters (984 feet) into Polish airspace and remained there for 42 seconds, the Polish military said.
Poland scrambled fighter jets and put ground forces and equipment on alert. “The nature of the incident indicates that Russia is once again testing the readiness of our air defense,” the command said.
Russia has not yet commented on the incident.
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on September 17 that Russia is planning “hybrid” strikes using missiles and drones against countries that support Ukraine. He claimed that “there is a real risk that drones or other types of missiles may fly into the territory of one or more NATO countries on the eastern flank, even cause destruction.”

Manfred D, former head of cabinet to ex-intelligence chief August Hanning, was taken into custody on charges of aiding and abetting treason. He is accused of obtaining classified BND documents and passing them to Hanning in exchange for payment since 2010.
Following the arrest of former BND chief August Hanning on Tuesday in what has turned out to be Germany's biggest espionage scandal, his long-standing confidant and former head of cabinet Manfred D has now also been taken into custody.

Federal prosecutors accuse both men of having used state secrets over many years to support private consulting activities and foreign interests, a crime that constitutes treason.
Manfred D, 64, has been charged with aiding and abetting and remains in pre-trial detention, while Hanning is being brought before an investigating judge,…

On October 7, 2006, Anna Politkovskaya, a journalist with Novaya Gazeta, was killed in the elevator of her apartment building in Moscow. Six people were convicted in connection with the murder, but her colleagues are convinced that whoever ordered the killing was never found.
In the last years of her life, Politkovskaya worked closely with and was close friends with human rights activist Natalya Estemirova. Estemirova introduced the journalist to the subjects of her future reports from Chechnya and helped her get into places other Moscow journalists could not reach. “She was her Virgil, a guide through all the circles of hell,” is how human rights activist Alexander…

Kremlinul a declarat miercuri că testarea de către Franța a unei rachete cu capacitate nucleară a demonstrat că Europa își construiește identitatea de apărare în jurul confruntării cu Rusia, calificând această strategie drept „o cale fără ieșire”, relatează Reuters .
Marți, președintele francez Emmanuel Macron a salutat testul rachetei balistice lansate de pe un submarin în largul coastelor Bretaniei ca fiind un mesaj „transmis clar și răspicat către oricine trebuie să-l primească”, fără a menționa în mod direct Rusia.
Lansarea a avut loc pe fondul tensiunilor accentuate legate de războiul din Ucraina, de securitatea europeană…

Two people were killed and seven others injured in a Russian attack on Kremenchuk, Poltava region, according to preliminary reports.
Head of the Poltava Regional Military Administration Volodymyr Diakivnych said this in a Telegram post , according to Ukrinform.


"According to preliminary information, two people were killed. My condolences to their families and loved ones.



Another seven people were injured," Diakivnych wrote.


He added that the rescue operation was ongoing.

titulekPuvodni: Bývalý ředitel německé rozvědky je podezřelý ze špionáže. Únik může být historický
shrnuti: Pokud se obvinění potvrdí, šlo by o jeden z největších špionážních případů v dějinách spolkové republiky.

vyrez.text:
Bývalý ředitel německé rozvědky je podezřelý ze špionáže. Únik může být historický — Deník N
Policie odváží zatčeného Manfreda D., bývalého vedoucího kanceláře ředitele německé tajné služby BND Augusta Hanninga. Ten byl zatčen také. Foto: Rene Priebe, DPA/ČTK
Pokud se obvinění potvrdí, šlo by o jeden z největších špionážních případů v dějinách spolkové republiky.
Více o poslechu Deníku N
V německé zahraniční rozvědce se rýsuje případ vlastizrady nevídaných rozměrů. Německá média předpovídají, že bezprecedentní skandál může otřást celou tajnou službou.
O co jde?
Podle informací investigativního týmu WDR, NDR a Süddeutsche Zeitung (SZ) bývalého ředitele Spolkové zpravodajské služby (BND) Augusta Hanninga vyšetřují kvůli podezření ze špionáže poškozující stát a kvůli zpravodajské činnosti.
Podle obvinění po skončení kariéry celé roky nelegálně získával tajné informace z tajné služby, která shromažďuje a vyhodnocuje informace o zahraniční, bezpečnostní a hospodářské politice.
Byl zatčen ve svém domě v Nordwalde u Münsteru na západě Německa.
Týdeník Spiegel napsal, že v 6.41 policisté přijeli a v 8.58 ho odvezli v černém mikrobusu.
V Bavorsku pak byl zadržen i další bývalý vysoký…

Volgograd Governor Andrey Bocharov said there had been a “massive drone attack on industrial infrastructure” but did not specify which facilities were targeted. Eyewitnesses posted photos and videos of a large fire in the area around the Volgograd refinery.
Ukrainian drones previously attacked the Volgograd refinery on May 29 and July 31, Reuters reported. According to the website of its owner, Lukoil, the refinery can process about 14 million metric tons of crude oil a year — roughly 5% of Russia’s total refining volume.

Germany’s Federal Prosecutor’s Office said it detained August Hanning, the former head of the country’s Federal Intelligence Service (BND), on suspicion of espionage and attempted treason. His former bureau chief, Manfred D., was detained along with him.
Hanning led the BND from December 1998 to November 2005. Investigators said that in 2010, he arranged for Manfred D. to pass him classified intelligence agency information in exchange for money. By 2022, Hanning had obtained roughly 2,000 internal BND documents, including materials on Iran’s nuclear program and the Russian armed forces.
In one instance, he used the documents to prepare an analytical report for an officer of a foreign intelligence service, though it is not clear which country was involved. Süddeutsche Zeitung, NDR, and WDR reported that this episode was not connected to Russia.

Former German spy chief arrested for espionage and treason - BBC News
Image source, AP
Image caption, Agents arrested August Hanning (pictured from 2015) at his home on Tuesday
By Olivia Ireland
Published
3 hours ago
Former German spy chief August Hanning has been arrested on suspicion of espionage, treason and obtaining classified information for a foreign power, the German Federal Prosecutor's Office says.
Hanning headed the Federal Intelligence Service (BND) from 1998 to 2005 and has since been working as a private consultant.
Prosecutors allege that he used classified intelligence to "draft an analysis" for one foreign intelligence service and maintained contact with another foreign spying service. Investigators have not disclosed which foreign powers were involved.
Police also arrested former BND employee Manfred D, accusing him of passing Hanning about 2,000 classified documents for money.
Manfred D, who was Hanning's bureau chief and remained in the BND until this year, is charged with aiding and abetting attempted treason and treasonous espionage.
Local media reported Hanning was arrested at his home in Nordwalde near Münster while Manfred D was arrested in Bavaria.…

vyrez.text:
Former German spy chief arrested for treason and espionage – POLITICO
Skip to main content
Advertisement
BERLIN — A former head of Germany’s foreign intelligence agency was arrested early Tuesday in connection with an investigation into suspected espionage and attempted treason, according to the German Federal Prosecutors Office.
An informant allegedly provided August Hanning, the former head of the foreign intelligence agency, or BND, with nearly two thousand documents, many of them classified, according to a statement from federal prosecutors . In one case, Hanning used classified information provided by an informant identified as Manfred D. to create an analysis for an employee of a foreign intelligence service, according the prosecutors office.
“The accused Hanning is under strong suspicion of espionage constituting treason,” the prosecutors’ statement read.
The allegations will amount to a huge embarrassment for Germany’s foreign intelligence agency, which Hanning ran between 1998 and 2005.
This is a developing story.

shrnuti: Businessman Oleg Varyukhin, who traveled to Russia after living in Ukraine for 27 years, has been charged with treason for paying Ukraine’s mandatory military levy into its state budget, Mediazona reported.

vyrez.text:
Russia has brought its first known treason case based on tax payments to Ukraine — Meduza
Skip to main content
Russia has brought its first known treason case based on tax payments to Ukraine
October 5, 2026, 7:32 pm
Source: Mediazona
Businessman Oleg Varyukhin, who traveled to Russia after living in Ukraine for 27 years, has been charged with treason for paying Ukraine’s mandatory military levy into its state budget, Mediazona reported.
Varyukhin was detained in May 2026. In early August, his lawyer, Yuri Shel, said the treason charge stemmed from tax payments in Ukraine. At the time, it was unclear which tax the Russian authorities had taken issue with.
Officers from Russia’s Federal Security Service found records of the tax payments on Varyukhin’s phone during a search at the airport, his lawyer said.
Money transfers to support the Ukrainian army have previously led to treason prosecutions in Russia. But Varyukhin is the first person known to be prosecuted for treason for paying taxes into Ukraine’s state budget, Mediazona noted.

Italy’s Ustica enigma: Can French files solve mystery crash blamed on stray missile?
Analysis
Europe
France’s decision to share defence documents with the Italian judiciary has raised hopes of a breakthrough in investigations into the 1980 crash of a passenger jet near the island of Ustica, which a former Italian president claimed was mistakenly shot down by a French fighter jet. Sceptics caution that the files are unlikely to shed light on one of Italy’s most enduring mysteries, let alone reveal a culprit.

The reconstructed wreckage of Itavia Flight 870, which crashed near the island of Ustica in June 1980. © Emiliano Grillotti, AP
A rocky outpost of Italy in the Tyrrhenian Sea, the island of Ustica owes its name to the smouldering volcanic lava that gave its striking rock formations their dark hue.
For many Italians, however, the picturesque island is synonymous with a notorious plane crash that claimed 81 lives, and the intricate cover-up that buried its causes in a thick fog…

The 25-year-old, a dual UK-Iranian national, was arrested on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts under section 5 of the Terrorism Act 2006.
He was detained on Thursday in the borough of Westminster, London, where searches of two properties have now concluded.

titulekPuvodni: Ukraine tests EW system to protect heavy bomber drones and ground robots
shrnuti: Ukrainian defence company Aura-Ukraine has begun final tests of an electronic warfare (EW) system called Aura 3K mini, designed to protect heavy bomber drones and uncrewed ground vehicles.

vyrez.text:
Ukraine tests electronic warfare system to protect heavy bomber drones and ground robots | Ukrainska Pravda
Stock photo: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine
The Ukrainian defence company Aura-Ukraine has begun final tests of the Aura 3K mini, an electronic warfare (EW) system designed to protect heavy bomber drones.
Source: Dignitas Fund charity speaking to Ukrainska Pravda
Details: The device provides 360-degree protection through two broadband jammers operating in the 2.1-2.8 GHz range. They can jam Russian FPV drones without interfering with the platform's own Starlink communication link.
Advertisement:





The device weighs about 2.4 kg, according to Dignitas Fund, which is working on the EW system alongside the manufacturer. If the system's final tests are successful, it is slated for mass production.
Quote from the press service: "Testing of the system's radiation pattern will begin at the front in the coming days."
Photo: Characteristics and appearance of the Aura 3K Mini EW system. Dignitas

„Pevně věřím, že sbor je v perfektní kondici. Ale já chci tu kondici nejen udržet, ale ještě povýšit,“ uvedl v Interview ČT24 nový generální ředitel Hasičského záchranného sboru ČR Martin Legner. Do funkce jej jmenoval ministr vnitra Lubomír Metnar (ANO), který mu mimo jiné uložil i přípravu sboru na nové výzvy. Podle Legnera se hasiči připravují třeba na věci související s geopolitickou situací, zmínil také přípravy na válečný stav. Dosavadnímu řediteli sboru Vladimíru Vlčkovi skončil mandát v polovině července, funkční období generálního ředitele hasičů je pětileté. Pořadem provázel Daniel Takáč.
